Akathisia is an inner restlessness that drives repetitive movement, and the
movement usually fails to relieve it. That failure is the part worth
explaining, and accounts pitched at the receptor do not explain it. I am
building an active inference account instead, which asks whether the disorder
sits in how bodily prediction errors are turned into action rather than in the
motor system itself.

Aripiprazole is the pharmacological handle. The mechanism, and the predictions
that would separate this account from conventional motor and receptor-level
explanations, are being written up as a concept note. They go back on this page
when it carries a DOI.
